stem: What does a data retention policy define?

options.text: Who may edit or share a dashboard
How long data is kept before disposal
Which database engine stores the data
How often a report is refreshed

explanation: A retention policy sets keep and disposal periods for data. Dashboard editing, database engine choice and refresh frequency are unrelated to how long data is held.

stem: A United States company sells online to customers living in the European Union. Which regulation applies to those customers' personal data?

options.text: None, since the company is based elsewhere
Only the law of the state where the company operates
GDPR, based on where the data subjects live
Only the payment processor's terms

explanation: GDPR protects the personal data of people in the European Union regardless of where the company is based. Location of the company, state law or processor terms do not remove that duty.

stem: A customer asks a retailer to delete all of their personal data. With no legal reason to keep it, what should the retailer do under GDPR?

options.text: Mask the name but keep the rest
Move it to an archive indefinitely
Ignore the request until a breach occurs
Erase the data and confirm the deletion

explanation: GDPR gives individuals a right to erasure when no legal basis for keeping the data exists. Partial masking, indefinite archiving and ignoring the request all fail to honor it.

stem: Which THREE actions belong in the response to a confirmed data breach?

options.text: Contain the incident to stop further exposure
Delete the logs to save storage costs
Notify affected parties and regulators as required
Wait for the annual audit before disclosing
Preserve the logs as evidence for the investigation

explanation: Containment, timely notification and preserving evidence are core incident steps. Deleting logs destroys evidence and waiting delays duties.

stem: A national law requires health records of its citizens to stay inside the country. What does the company need in order to comply?

options.text: Storage in a data center within that jurisdiction
A longer retention period
A stronger password policy for all dashboard users
A faster network link

explanation: Jurisdictional rules on data residency dictate where data is physically stored. Retention length, passwords and bandwidth do not satisfy a location requirement.

stem: A team replicates its database to another region for resilience, but local law restricts where personal data may reside. What should they do?

options.text: Replicate to whichever region has the lowest monthly cost
Replicate only to regions the law permits
Skip the replication entirely
Replicate and disable the audit log

explanation: Replication copies must also satisfy jurisdictional rules, so targets must be limited to allowed regions. Choosing by cost or disabling logs ignores the rule, and skipping replication gives up resilience unnecessarily.

stem: Which standard governs the security of cardholder data?

options.text: The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
The General Data Protection Regulation
The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
The Sarbanes-Oxley Act

explanation: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard sets requirements for handling cardholder data. The other laws cover health privacy, personal data in Europe and financial reporting.

stem: Which TWO purposes does data classification serve?

options.text: Increasing the speed of queries
Determining the handling rules for each data type
Removing the need for an audit
Guiding which controls such as encryption apply
Choosing a chart type for each report

explanation: Classification sets how data is handled and which safeguards are used. It does not speed queries, replace audits or pick chart types.

stem: A merchant keeps card security codes in an order database after payment authorization. What does the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard require?

options.text: Encrypt the codes and store them for a year
Move the codes to a shared spreadsheet
Share the codes with the marketing team
Delete the codes after approval

explanation: The standard forbids retaining the card security code after authorization, even if encrypted. Keeping it for a year, copying it to a spreadsheet or sharing it all break that rule.

stem: What does an audit trail record?

options.text: Who accessed or changed data, and when
The color scheme used in each report
The size of each backup file
The expected growth of the dataset

explanation: An audit trail logs actions on data by user and time, which supports accountability. Color schemes, backup sizes and growth forecasts are not access records.

stem: A company labels its employee salary file as confidential rather than public. Which practice is this?

options.text: Replicating data across regions
Data classification
Data profiling
Data masking

explanation: Classification assigns sensitivity labels that drive handling rules. Replication copies data, profiling measures quality, and masking hides values.

stem: Which THREE rights does GDPR give individuals over their personal data?

options.text: Access to the data held about them
Unlimited retention by the company
Correction of inaccurate data
Free access to the company's reports
Erasure when no legal basis remains

explanation: GDPR provides rights of access, rectification and erasure. It gives no right to unlimited retention or to free access to company reports.

stem: A staff member finds that a spreadsheet of customer records was emailed to the wrong recipient. What is the best next step?

options.text: Delete the sent email and hope the recipient ignores it
Wait for the next scheduled audit
Report it through the incident process
Rename the file and resend it

explanation: A possible breach should go to the incident process promptly so the impact and notification duties can be judged. Hiding it, waiting for an audit or renaming and resending the file lets the risk grow.

stem: What is data ethics concerned with?

options.text: The server location and the hosting cost
The speed of query execution
The format of exported files
The fair and responsible use of data

explanation: Data ethics covers how data is collected and used with fairness, transparency and respect for people. Server location, speed and file formats are technical matters.

stem: A model that approves discounts uses postal codes that closely track a protected group, and results favor some neighborhoods. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Review the model for proxy-variable bias
Hide the postal codes from the report only
Increase the retention period
Add the model to the data dictionary only

explanation: Variables that stand in for protected traits can produce unfair outcomes, so the model should be reviewed for that bias. Hiding the field in a report, longer retention or documenting alone leave the unfairness in place.

stem: Which TWO organizations must follow the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard?

options.text: A merchant that accepts card payments
A company that only has a public website
A firm that stores only employee payroll files
A service provider that processes card data for others
A library that lends books

explanation: The standard applies to those who accept, store, process or transmit cardholder data. A public website, a firm that stores only employee payroll files and a lending library are outside its scope.

stem: Old invoices must be kept for seven years but are rarely read. Which storage choice fits best?

options.text: The fastest and most expensive tier available
A low-cost archive tier with access controls
A personal laptop with a local folder
A shared drive open to all staff

explanation: Rarely used records that must be retained suit cheap archival storage that is still protected. Premium tiers waste money, and laptops or open shared drives expose the data.

stem: A customer file has passed its retention period, with no legal hold and no business need. What should the data steward do?

options.text: Keep it in case it is needed someday
Copy it to a second region
Securely dispose of the data per the policy
Reclassify it as public

explanation: Once the period has ended and no hold applies, policy calls for secure disposal. Keeping it extends risk, replicating it adds copies, and making it public exposes personal data.

stem: An external auditor asks for evidence of who changed a financial table last quarter. What should the team provide?

options.text: The data dictionary
The dashboard mockups and style guide
The latest snapshot
The access records kept for that table

explanation: Access records show who changed data and when. A dictionary, mockups or a snapshot show structure, design or content but not the people behind the changes.

stem: Which TWO factors matter when assessing jurisdictional requirements for a dataset?

options.text: The brand and version of the reporting tool in use
The file format of the export
The location where the data is stored
The color scheme of the dashboards
The residency of the people the data describes

explanation: Storage location and the residence of data subjects determine which laws apply. Tool brand, file format and color scheme do not.

stem: Sort each item into the classification level it should carry.

items.text: Staff directory with desk phone numbers
Annual report posted on the website

explanation: Information already released is public, material for staff use only is internal, and data whose exposure would harm individuals or the company is confidential.

partExplanations.org: Meant for staff only, but low harm if seen.
partExplanations.cards: Payment card data is highly sensitive.
partExplanations.report: Posted on the website, so public.

stem: Sort each requirement into the compliance concept it illustrates.

items.text: Delete invoices seven years after the account closes
Keep residents' data on servers inside their home country
Review who opened payroll files last quarter
Tell regulators within a set time after a data breach
Archive emails for exactly three years
Sample access logs to prove controls were followed

explanation: Retention fixes how long data is kept, jurisdictional rules tie data to a place, audits verify what happened, and incident reporting sets notification duties.

partExplanations.i1: A fixed keep-then-delete period is retention.
partExplanations.i2: Where data may live is a jurisdictional rule.
partExplanations.i3: Reviewing past access is an audit activity.
partExplanations.i4: Notifying regulators after a breach is incident reporting.
partExplanations.i5: A set storage period is retention.
partExplanations.i6: Examining logs to prove compliance is an audit.

stem: Match each scenario to the data governance concept it describes.

prompts.text: A hospital keeps a second copy of its records in another region so a flood cannot destroy them.
A team debates whether an algorithm that scores loan applicants treats groups fairly.
A company must follow European rules on how it handles data about people in Europe.
An analyst labels a dataset as restricted so only approved staff can open it.

explanation: Replication copies data for resilience, ethics asks whether use is fair, GDPR governs the data of people in Europe, and classification labels sensitivity.

partExplanations.p1: A second copy in another region is replication.
partExplanations.p2: Fairness of data use is a data ethics question.
partExplanations.p3: GDPR covers the personal data of people in Europe.

stem: This access log extract was prepared for an audit. Select every entry that should be flagged for investigation.

nodes.text: Contractor with no approved request exports 40,000 customer rows
Staff member edits own display name

spots.name: Contractor with no approved request exports 40,000 customer rows
Staff member edits own display name

explanation: A bulk export by a contractor, a sign-in from a disabled account, and a sales user in payroll data are all outside expected access. The scheduled report, backup and a display name edit are routine.

partExplanations.export: A bulk export of personal data by a contractor with no approved request needs investigation.
partExplanations.disabled: A disabled account should never sign in.
partExplanations.display: Users may edit their own profile.
partExplanations.payroll: Sales staff have no need for payroll data.
